name: Amara Ngozi-Szilveszter
role: Retired secondary school teacher and current community education volunteer; grandmother raising two grandchildren
location: Washburn Commons — apartment block C, and the Commons community center basement classroom, near Halsted and Chicago Ave
description:
Amara Ngozi-Szilveszter is the kind of woman who makes a room feel organized just by walking into it. She's tall and angular, her natural hair kept in a close-cropped fade that's gone entirely silver, and she has the habit of standing with her arms folded and her chin slightly elevated that every one of her former students would recognize from forty meters away. Her dark skin is unaugmented save for a small bioluminescent spiral — blue-white — behind her right ear, a retirement gift she gave herself after three decades of institutional dress codes. She wears sensible layers and always has two pens in her breast pocket, a habit from the years before all writing went digital.

Amara taught mathematics and systems-thinking at Washburn Commons Secondary for thirty-one years, surviving four different corponation educational management contracts and two restructuring purges. She retired with a modest pension and immediate custody of her two grandchildren — Prax, eleven, and Liesel, eight — after her daughter's commitment to a Helix Biosystems experimental labor program took her away for what was supposed to be eighteen months and has now been three years. Amara does not discuss this with people she doesn't trust. She runs a free after-school tutoring program out of the community center basement three afternoons a week, partly because she needs to be useful and partly because she's keeping an eye on every child in a two-block radius as a matter of survival strategy.

core_fears: That her daughter is never coming back and she'll have to explain it to the children
That the educational systems she spent her life working within were always designed to produce compliance rather than capacity
core_desires: To give Prax and Liesel a genuine skill set for navigating the city, not just surviving it
To see one of her tutoring students do something the system didn't plan for them
coping_mechanisms: Structure and routine — meals at the same time, lessons prepared in advance, every problem approached as a curriculum design challenge
blind_spots: Can be condescending to adults she decides aren't thinking rigorously enough
psychology.secret: She's been in contact with a labor rights advocate who believes Helix Biosystems' experimental programs have a much lower return rate than officially reported. She's started quietly documenting everything she can about her daughter's contract and circumstances. She hasn't told the children she's afraid their mother is dead.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and structured — she still teaches when she talks, scaffolding ideas for maximum retention whether she means to or not; slips into warmth in unguarded moments
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and well-paced with a teacher's projection; can command a room without raising her voice
verbal_tics: 'What's the actual claim being made here'
Pausing mid-sentence to let someone finish their own thought
example_lines: 'You're telling me what you felt. I believe you. Now tell me what you observed — those are different things and both matter.'
'Three years is not eighteen months. I can do that subtraction and so can you.'

story_hooks: Amara's labor-rights contact has gone silent after getting close to something in the Helix Biosystems documentation — she needs someone trustworthy to make a delivery to a secondary contact she's never met

One of her tutoring students has demonstrated a mathematical aptitude that a Sterling-Nakamura talent scout has noticed, and the scout's contract offer is designed to benefit Sterling-Nakamura far more than the child
narrative_function: Quest giver and community connector; knows every child in a wide radius and therefore knows what's happening at street level that adults aren't saying out loud. Her entanglement with Helix Biosystems through her daughter's contract gives her a motivated stake in stories involving that corponation.
augmentations: Bioluminescent spiral dermal implant (behind right ear, blue-white; cosmetic only). Standard retinal display for reading — the cheap consumer model, not corporate-grade. No other augmentations.
daily_life: School-run for Prax and Liesel in the morning, then community center administration or supply scrounging, then afternoon tutoring sessions; evenings are homework, dinner, and what she calls 'the news hour' where she reads actual text journalism to the kids and makes them argue with it.
affiliation: Washburn Commons Community Council; former Meridian Teachers' Collective (retired); Helix Biosystems dependency (through daughter's contract)

decision_rules: Understand the system before working around it — or through it
Don't take help from anyone until you understand what they want
escalation_ladder: Direct statement of the problem and what she needs
Public documentation and community council escalation
Deploying every contact she has built in thirty-one years of teaching

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Courteous and evaluating — she has a teacher's quick read of people and is testing competence and character simultaneously
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm, irreverent, capable of real laughter; shows up with food

stress_responses.medium: Focuses intensely on the controllable — the children's routine, the classroom, the lesson
stress_responses.high: Becomes very still and very direct; stops performing patience

contradictions: Teaches critical thinking as liberation while structuring her grandchildren's lives with strict routine
Deeply skeptical of corponations but hasn't broken her daughter's Helix contract because she still hopes it means something
habits: Pens in breast pocket even though she rarely uses physical writing
Makes tea for anyone who sits down in her classroom regardless of why they came
Reads the children a different city history every Sunday
breaking_points: Any threat to the children, explicit or implied
Someone trying to exploit one of her tutoring students

timeline.event: Began teaching mathematics at Washburn Commons Secondary
Survived first Tessera educational management contract restructuring
Assumed custody of grandchildren Prax and Liesel after daughter entered Helix program
Began documenting Helix labor program return rates

physical_description.build: Tall and angular, lean-muscled from decades of standing and moving through classrooms; posture still carries the straightness of institutional discipline, though age has introduced a slight forward inclination at the shoulders
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped fade, meticulously maintained, revealing the clean geometry of her skull
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with faint amber undertones from standard consumer retinal display overlay (visible as a thin luminescent ring around the iris in low light)
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep brown with warm undertones, characteristic of West African heritage; shows the weathering of 67 years and significant UV exposure from pre-GLMZ childhood
physical_description.complexion: Face bears the map of her life: crow's feet from squinting at chalkboards and reading small text, a thin vertical scar along her left jawline (accident with a door frame, 2187), hands bearing the ink stains of someone who still writes by hand despite digital availability. Skin is unaugmented and well-maintained; minimal makeup, sharp cheekbones that prominence with age
distinguishing_marks: Small vertical scar along left jawline, approximately 3cm, pale and well-healed
Bioluminescent spiral dermal implant behind right ear, blue-white, 4cm diameter, glows softly in darkness — visible when hair is pulled back or in profile
Two small burn marks on her right inner forearm from a classroom incident, now faint but still visible on close inspection
Callused fingertips and palm creases darker than surrounding skin from decades of writing and chalk dust
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent spiral behind right ear (cosmetic, retirement gift to herself). Faint luminescent ring around pupils indicating standard consumer-grade retinal display. No other visible chrome or subdermal plating; deliberately maintains non-augmented appearance as marker of her tier and values
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with arms often folded across chest or hands clasped at solar plexus—a posture from decades of classroom management. Moves with deliberate efficiency, no wasted motion; walks with spine straight despite age-related stiffening. Has a habit of tilting her head slightly when listening, chin elevated, eyes tracking movement. When sitting, she occupies minimal space, feet flat on floor, back against chair
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 practical utilitarian: layered cotton and synthetic-blend clothing in muted earth tones (charcoal, sage, cream, rust). Always wears a sleeveless overshirt or vest as outer layer—functional pockets, durable weave. Sensible non-slip shoes suitable for classroom floors. Two pens always in breast pocket (old habit, pre-digital era). A thin silver bracelet on her left wrist (gift from her father, 2150s). No jewelry beyond this; no corpo logos or status markers. Clothing shows wear and careful repair—patches on elbows, reinforced seams—not from poverty but from intentional durability ethic
